Subject: Tenant segmentation and data governance questions (RFI)

Hi Logan / Grace,

Thanks for taking the time to engage on our RFI. As we finalize internal approvals, a few focused questions remain around tenant isolation and data governance for Redwood Private deployed into our VPCs:

1) Can you describe how tenant logical separation is enforced at the compute and storage layers?
2) Do you support per-tenant encryption keys (tenant-scoped KMS keys) and customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations?
3) What audit evidence can you provide that shows separation (logs, KV cache delineation, access controls)?
4) For air-gapped/offline installations, what artifacts can we review to validate the installation process and file integrity checks?

If possible, please attach a short matrix mapping your controls to our requirements and a sample network diagram we can circulate to our infra team. Also let us know SLA implications for tenant-level disruptions.

Appreciate a reply by 2028-07-21 EOD if feasible.

Best,
Sanjay
Sanjay Mehta
Director, IT Security
Tidal Health Systems

Subject: Re: Tenant segmentation and data governance questions (RFI)

Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear set of questions. High-level answers below and I attached a short matrix and a sample network isolation diagram as requested. More detail from our infra team follows in a subsequent message.

1) Logical separation: Redwood Private implements tenant isolation via per-tenant namespaces at the runtime layer, separated persistent stores per tenant (configurable per deployment), and strict process-level ACLs. When deployed into your VPC, we provision tenancy-scoped storage paths and service accounts that are mapped to your identity provider.

2) Tenant-scoped keys: Yes — our Private package supports customer-managed keys. We integrate with cloud KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault) and on-prem HSMs via PKCS#11. You may configure a unique CMK for each tenant; key access is limited to the node-level process with minimal privilege.

3) Audit evidence: We can provide time-series logs showing access boundaries, KV cache access logs by tenant id, and an access-control matrix exported from our control plane. We also produce immutable operation logs (tamper-evident) that can be forwarded to your SIEM.

4) Air-gapped artifacts: For offline installs we produce signed installation bundles with checksums and a guide for SMR (secure media transfer). We include SBOM exports and a signed runtime attestation you can verify with our public key.

Next steps: attached are the tenant_segmentation_matrix.csv and sample_network_isolation.pdf. Grace will add technical detail on key management and logging format in the next email.

Regards,

Logan Wright
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachments: tenant_segmentation_matrix.csv; sample_network_isolation.pdf

Hi Sanjay — following up with the technical specifics you asked for.

Compute & storage enforcement:
- Runtime namespaces: each tenant runs in an isolated runtime namespace; inter-tenant requests are blocked by the routing layer.
- Disk/storage: persistent model caches and user artifacts are placed on tenant-scoped mounts. We support either separate volumes per tenant or logically partitioned directories with filesystem ACLs.

Key management:
- Per-tenant keys supported. Options:
  * Cloud KMS CMK per tenant (AWS KMS, Azure KV)
  * Customer HSM with PKCS#11 integration (per-tenant key slots)
- Keys are never exported in cleartext; decryption operations occur on the node with HSM-backed signing when configured.

Logging & audit format:
- Audit logs include tenant_id and request_id fields. Logs can be streamed to your S3/Blob storage or pushed to SIEM via syslog.
- KV cache events include origin IP, node id, tenant id and timestamp; sample extracts are in the attached evidence bundle.

Runtime attestation & integrity:
- We sign release artifacts with an offline private key; installer verifies checksums and signature.
- For air-gapped installs we provide a hashed SBOM and a signed attestation (see redwood_runtime_attestation.pdf).

Operational SLA note: tenant-level isolation issues are treated as high priority incidents and will follow a dedicated runbook; we can discuss contractual SLA credits based on impact scope in your procurement thread.

Let me know if you want a short demo showing the audit exports in your SIEM.

— Grace
Grace O'Connor
Principal Product Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
